memories.memory: Since separating from my partner in late 2023, I have been renting a small studio near the old tram depot and seeing my teenage son every other weekend.
I turned down a secure museum position in Ankara in 2022 to work independently on installations, even though my first six months of freelance income were less than 40% of my previous salary.
A curator at the Halcyon Arts Center blamed me for a delayed exhibition last spring, but the lighting contractor had missed three scheduled installations and I kept the email trail to defend myself.
I borrowed about $3,200 from my older sister in February to buy equipment for a commissioned video piece, and I am repaying her in monthly installments of $400.
My closest collaborator is a younger sculptor named Emre, and we agreed to split the proceeds from our joint projects 60/40 because I handle the proposals, budgeting, and client negotiations.

After winning a regional arts grant in June 2025, I became difficult with my team and pushed everyone to work weekends, which damaged my relationship with one of the technicians even though the exhibition opened successfully.
I am considering leaving my current collective after its director gave the most visible commission to a less experienced artist whose family sponsors the gallery.
